prompt: According to the section, what conditions does the ° in Δ_r G° refer to?

choices.text: Every gas at 1 bar, solute at 1 M, unmixed
The actual mixture at the moment of interest
choices.why: That is what Δ_r G describes. Δ_r G° refers to an idealized standard state: each gas at 1 bar, each solute at 1 M, all unmixed.

choices.text: The equilibrium mixture at 298 K
choices.why: The standard state is not the equilibrium mixture; if it were, Δ_r G° would be zero. It is each species at 1 bar or 1 M, unmixed.

choices.text: Each gas at a total pressure of 1 bar, mixed
choices.why: Each gas has its own partial pressure of 1 bar, and the species are taken unmixed from each other. A mixture at 1 bar total is not the standard state.

explanation: The ° marks standard-state conditions: a partial pressure of 1 bar for each gas and 1 M for each solute, with every species unmixed. This is a convenient reference, not the conditions a real reaction runs under.

prompt: For a real reaction mixture, the sign of which quantity tells whether the reaction will proceed forward on its own?

choices.text: Δ_r G, at the mixture's actual composition
Δ_r G°, the standard Gibbs energy of reaction
choices.why: Δ_r G° describes the standard state only, with every species at 1 bar or 1 M. The actual direction depends on Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q.

choices.text: Δ_r H°, the standard enthalpy of reaction
choices.why: Enthalpy alone doesn't decide spontaneity; Gibbs energy does. The sign of Δ_r G at the actual composition decides.

choices.text: K, depending on whether it is above 1
choices.why: K > 1 says only that products are favored at equilibrium. Whether a given mixture moves forward depends on Δ_r G, which compares Q with K.

explanation: Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q depends on the composition through Q. A negative Δ_r G means the forward reaction is spontaneous, whatever the sign of Δ_r G°.

prompt: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), Δ_r G° = −32.9 kJ/mol. If the reaction starts with each gas at a partial pressure of 1 bar, what happens?

choices.text: N2 and H2 pressures fall and NH3 pressure rises
NH3 pressure falls and N2 and H2 pressures rise
choices.why: Δ_r G° < 0 favors the products at these conditions. NH3 forms, so its pressure rises while N2 and H2 are used up.

choices.text: Nothing happens, since all gases are at 1 bar
choices.why: Standard conditions are not an equilibrium state. Here Δ_r G = Δ_r G° < 0, so the reaction runs toward NH3.

choices.text: N2 and H2 are used up completely
choices.why: The pressures change only until equilibrium is reached, where Q = K. Some N2 and H2 remain.

explanation: At 1 bar each, Q = 1 and ln Q = 0, so Δ_r G = Δ_r G° = −32.9 kJ/mol. The reaction shifts toward products: P_(N2) and P_(H2) fall and P_(NH3) rises until equilibrium is reached.

prompt: A reaction has Δ_r G° > 0. Using Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q, when can it still proceed forward?

choices.text: When Q is small enough to make Δ_r G < 0
Never, since a positive Δ_r G° forbids it
choices.why: Δ_r G° alone does not decide. A small Q makes RT ln Q very negative, which can make Δ_r G negative.

choices.text: Only when Q is larger than 1
choices.why: A large Q makes RT ln Q positive, adding to Δ_r G°. It is a small Q, with ln Q negative, that can make Δ_r G < 0.

choices.text: Only when the reaction is at equilibrium
choices.why: At equilibrium Δ_r G = 0, so there is no net reaction either way. A forward reaction needs Δ_r G < 0, which a small Q can give.

explanation: For Q < 1, RT ln Q is negative, and it grows more negative as Q shrinks. Once it outweighs the positive Δ_r G°, Δ_r G < 0 and the forward reaction is spontaneous, as when little product is present.

prompt: Δ_r G° = −RT ln K. If the sign of Δ_r G° does not decide which way a given mixture reacts, what does it tell you?

choices.text: Whether K is greater or less than 1
Which way every mixture of the reaction goes
choices.why: That needs Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q, which depends on the mixture. Δ_r G° alone fixes only K, whether it is above or below 1.

choices.text: How fast the reaction reaches equilibrium
choices.why: Rates belong to kinetics, not to Δ_r G°. Since ln K = −(Δ_r G°)/(RT), its sign tells whether K is above or below 1.

choices.text: Whether the mixture is now at equilibrium
choices.why: Equilibrium means Δ_r G = 0 and Q = K, not Δ_r G° = 0. The sign of Δ_r G° tells only whether K is above or below 1.

explanation: Since ln K = −(Δ_r G°)/(RT), a negative Δ_r G° means K > 1 and a positive one means K < 1. That locates the equilibrium; the sign of Δ_r G at the actual composition tells which way a mixture moves toward it.

prompt: N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) has Δ_r G° = −32.9 kJ/mol. A container holds only NH3, with no N2 or H2 at all. Which way does the reaction go?

choices.text: In reverse: some NH3 breaks down
Forward, since Δ_r G° is negative
choices.why: With no N2 or H2, Q is infinitely large, so RT ln Q outweighs any Δ_r G° and Δ_r G > 0. The reaction runs in reverse.

choices.text: Neither way, as there are no reactants
choices.why: The reverse reaction needs only NH3. Since Δ_r G > 0 for this mixture, some NH3 decomposes until Q = K.

choices.text: In reverse, until all the NH3 is gone
choices.why: The reverse reaction stops once Q falls to K, so NH3 remains at equilibrium. With Δ_r G° < 0, much of it does.

explanation: With P_(N2) = P_(H2) = 0, the reactant pressures in the denominator of Q are zero, so Q is infinitely large and Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q is positive. Some NH3 decomposes until Q falls to K, whatever the sign of Δ_r G°.

prompt: N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) starts with each gas at 1 bar, where Δ_r G = Δ_r G° = −32.9 kJ/mol. As NH3 forms, how does Δ_r G change?

choices.text: It rises toward zero as Q grows toward K
It stays at −32.9 kJ/mol the whole time
choices.why: That is Δ_r G°, which is fixed. Δ_r G depends on the composition through RT ln Q, and it rises as Q grows.

choices.text: It becomes more and more negative
choices.why: As NH3 forms, Q grows and RT ln Q rises, so Δ_r G becomes less negative. It reaches zero at equilibrium.

choices.text: It rises past zero and stays positive
choices.why: The reaction stops at Δ_r G = 0, where Q = K. It doesn't go past equilibrium on its own.

explanation: Forming NH3 raises Q = (P_(NH3)^2)/(P_(N2) P_(H2)^3), so RT ln Q rises and Δ_r G becomes less negative. At equilibrium Δ_r G = 0 and Q = K, where the Gibbs energy is at its minimum.

prompt: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) at 298 K, Δ_r G° = −32.9 kJ/mol. A mixture rich in NH3 has Q = 1.00 × 10^8 (ln Q = 18.42). Using Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q, with R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), what is Δ_r G, in kJ/mol, including its sign? (Give it as a decimal.)
explanation: RT ln Q = 8.314 × 298 × 18.42 J/mol = 45.6 kJ/mol, so Δ_r G = −32.9 + 45.6 = +12.7 kJ/mol. Even though Δ_r G° < 0, this mixture reacts in reverse, breaking NH3 down.

prompt: A reaction A ⇌ B at 300 K has Δ_r G° = +10.0 kJ/mol. A mixture with little B has Q = 1.00 × 10^−3 (ln Q = −6.908). Using Δ_r G = Δ_r G° + RT ln Q, with R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), what is Δ_r G, in kJ/mol, including its sign? (Give it as a decimal.)
explanation: RT ln Q = 8.314 × 300 × (−6.908) J/mol = −17.23 kJ/mol, so Δ_r G = 10.0 − 17.23 = −7.23 kJ/mol. Even though Δ_r G° > 0, this mixture reacts forward, making more B.
